text:
## Description

Given an integer sequence, print the maximum sum of the distinct-value counts in three non-empty contiguous subarrays that partition the sequence in its original order.

## Preconditions

- **PRE-1 (Unverified).** Standard input supplies an integer \(N\) on the first line and \(N\) integers \(A_1,\ldots,A_N\) on the second line.
- **PRE-2 (Unverified).** The sequence length satisfies \(3 \le N \le 300{,}000\).
- **PRE-3 (Unverified).** Every sequence value satisfies \(1 \le A_k \le N\).

## Postconditions

- **POST-1 (Unverified).** Standard output contains a single integer equal to the maximum score over all cut pairs \(1 \le i < j \le N-1\). The cuts define the subarrays at positions \(1\) through \(i\), \(i+1\) through \(j\), and \(j+1\) through \(N\).
- **POST-2 (Unverified).** Each distinct value contributes one to the score of each subarray in which it occurs, regardless of its frequency there.
- **POST-3 (Unverified).** The answer is between \(3\) and \(N\), inclusive. For \(N=3\), the only legal partition has three singleton subarrays, so the answer is \(3\).

## Test suggestions

- Check \(N=3\) with the sequence \(1,3,1\). Expect \(3\) (PRE-2, PRE-3, POST-3).
- Check an all-equal sequence of length greater than three and an all-distinct sequence. Expect \(3\) and \(N\), respectively (POST-1, POST-2).
- Check both supplied samples for outputs \(5\) and \(9\). The first sample has multiple maximizing partitions and still produces one integer (PRE-1, POST-1).
- Check \(N=300{,}000\) with all entries equal to \(N\). Expect \(3\) (PRE-2, PRE-3, POST-2).

## Unspecified behavior

- Behavior for input that violates PRE-1, PRE-2, or PRE-3 is unspecified.
- No choice among maximizing cut pairs is specified. The score is the only requested output.
